transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At 9 years old, an Indesit washing machine can often be worth repairing if the fault is mechanical rather than electronic. The most common reasons for a drum that fills and drains but doesn't spin are a broken drive belt or worn motor brushes—both of which are relatively inexpensive to fix. To determine the next step safely, please unplug the machine and remove the rear panel (typically held by two screws at the top). Look inside for a black rubber belt connecting the small motor pulley to the large drum pulley. Is the belt still present and intact, or is it broken/missing?

Right, I've pulled it out and taken the back panel off. The belt is on both pulleys and feels tight, so it doesn't look broken. What should I check next? I should mention I noticed a faint hot electrical smell from it a few weeks ago, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Regarding your question on whether it is worth fixing: mechanically, yes—Indesit machines are generally straightforward to repair. These are common wear parts on 9-year-old motors and are relatively inexpensive to replace. However, please note that due to the burning smell history, for safety reasons the machine must not be used again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. To help determine if this is a standard brush replacement or something more serious (like a motor winding fault), I need your model number. Could you check the rating plate inside the door rim or on the back of the door and tell me the full model number?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I've had a look at the label inside the door and it reads IWC 71252. I can't make out anything more than that at the moment. I'll keep it switched off and unplugged as you say.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Thank you for checking that. On these Indesit machines, the brushes are small blocks of graphite inside the motor; as they wear down, they can spark (causing the smell) and eventually stop transferring power to the motor. To confirm this safely: with the machine unplugged, look at the back of the motor (the round metal part near where the belt is). There should be two small plastic caps on the side or back. If you can gently remove them, you can pull out the carbon brushes. Are they still long and solid, or are they very short (less than 1cm) or broken? Please remember: because of the burning smell history, do not attempt to run the machine again until a qualified engineer has inspected it.
I've taken the brushes out as you described. One is very short and blackened or charred at the tip, and the other is a bit longer. The machine is still unplugged. What does that tell us?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
That tells us exactly why the drum isn't turning: one of the carbon brushes has worn down so much that it can no longer transfer electricity to the motor. Because there was a burning smell, this indicates an active electrical fault. Even though replacing the carbon brushes is a relatively inexpensive fix (and often something owners can do themselves if they are confident), the machine must not be used again until it has been inspected by a qualified engineer to ensure there isn't further damage to the motor windings or wiring. To answer your original question: at 9 years old, this is likely worth fixing if you get the brushes replaced and have the electrical safety checked. However, do not attempt to run the machine again yourself.
